title: Append at the end
summary: Walk to the last node, then hang the new one on it. Why this costs O(n).

checkpoints.text: The list was empty, so the new node becomes the first node. `headRef` holds the address of `head` in `main` (`&head`), so `*headRef = newNode;` changes `main`'s own `head`.
Appending 30. The list only remembers its first node, so `last` has to start at the front and walk.

The walk stopped at the node whose `next` was NULL, and the new node now hangs on it. For a list of n nodes the walk takes about n hops, so appending is O(n). Inserting at the front needs no walk at all: O(1).
10 -> 20 -> 30 -> NULL: the values came out in the order they were appended.
`freeList` deletes the nodes one by one from the front. It saves `head->next` before each `delete`, because a deleted node must not be read again.
